confirm_payment_intent.description: Charge a payment set up with Create a payment to a saved card or other payment method.
confirm_payment_intent.name: confirm_payment_intent

parameters.description: The payment to confirm.
parameters.name: payment_intent_id

parameters.description: The saved card or other payment method to charge, which starts with pm_. In test mode, pm_card_visa is a test card.
parameters.name: payment_method

returns.description: The payment, with its status now succeeded.

create_customer.description: Add a customer to Stripe with their email and, if you like, their name, phone number and a note.
create_customer.name: create_customer

parameters.description: The customer's email address.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: The customer's full name or business name.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: A note about the customer. Only your team sees it, in Stripe.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: The customer's phone number.
parameters.name: phone

returns.description: The new customer: their id, email, name and the rest of what Stripe keeps about them.

create_payment_intent.description: Set up a card payment of any amount, optionally for a customer. No money moves until the payment is confirmed with Confirm a payment.
create_payment_intent.name: create_payment_intent

parameters.description: The amount in cents, not dollars: 5000 is $50.00. For a currency with no cents, such as yen, the whole amount.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: The three-letter currency code, such as usd or eur.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: The customer paying, if you know them.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: A short note saying what the payment is for.
parameters.name: description

returns.description: The new payment: its id, amount in cents, currency and status.

create_payment_link.description: Make a link to a Stripe checkout page where anyone can pay a price.
create_payment_link.name: create_payment_link

parameters.description: The price the link charges.
parameters.name: price_id

parameters.description: How many the customer buys. Leave empty for one.
parameters.name: quantity

returns.description: The new payment link: its id and its url to share.

create_price.description: Set what a product costs, once or on a repeating schedule such as monthly.
create_price.name: create_price

parameters.description: The product this price is for.
parameters.name: product_id

parameters.description: The price in cents, not dollars: 5000 is $50.00. For a currency with no cents, such as yen, the whole amount.
parameters.name: unit_amount

parameters.description: The three-letter currency code, such as usd or eur.
parameters.name: currency

parameters.description: For a repeating price, how often the customer pays: day, week, month or year. Leave empty for a one-off price.
parameters.name: interval

parameters.description: How many intervals between payments. For example, 3 with a monthly interval charges every 3 months.
parameters.name: interval_count

returns.description: The new price: its id, amount in cents, currency and how often it repeats.

create_product.description: Add something you sell. Give it a price with Create a price before you charge for it.
create_product.name: create_product

parameters.description: The product's name, as customers see it.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What the product is, as customers see it.
parameters.name: description

returns.description: The new product: its id, name and other details.

list_customers.description: List your newest customers, most recent first.
list_customers.name: list_customers

parameters.description: How many customers to list, at most 100.
parameters.name: limit

items.description: A customer: their id, email, name and other details.

list_invoices.description: List the invoices created in a period, with each invoice's number, customer, amount due and paid in dollars (or your currency), status and due date. Use it for a daily or weekly invoice summary or to chase unpaid invoices.
list_invoices.name: list_invoices

parameters.description: The start of the period.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: The end of the period. Leave empty to run the period up to now.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Only invoices in this state.
parameters.name: status

invoices.description: Each invoice, with its id, number, status, amount due and amount paid in dollars (or your currency), currency, customer name and email, the day it was created and when it is due (YYYY-MM-DD), and a link the customer can open.

list_payments.description: List the payments made in a period, with how many there were, the total in dollars (or your currency) and who paid the most. Use it for a weekly or monthly sales summary.
list_payments.name: list_payments

parameters.description: The start of the period. Required unless you use Paid in the last days.
parameters.name: created_after

parameters.description: Beta. Only payments from the last this many whole days up to now: 7 on a Friday at 4pm is the week since last Friday at 4pm, so two weekly reports never count a payment twice. Use it for a daily, weekly or monthly summary instead of working out the dates in earlier steps. Paid on or after wins when given.
parameters.name: created_in_last_days

parameters.description: Beta. Only payments from the whole of last month or this month so far, for a monthly report that runs on the 1st: no dates to work out in earlier steps, and the month's name comes back as period (October 2026). Replaces the dates above when chosen.
parameters.name: calendar_month

parameters.description: The end of the period. Leave empty to run the period up to now.
parameters.name: created_before

parameters.description: Only payments in this state. Succeeded payments are the ones that brought in money.
parameters.name: status

currency.description: The currency the total is in (the first payment's).

payments.description: Each payment, with its id, status, amount in cents (5000 is $50.00), currency, when it was made, who paid (name and email) and its description.

period.description: The calendar month reported, such as October 2026, when Calendar month is chosen; blank otherwise.

top_customer.description: Who paid the most in the period, by name or email.

top_customer_total.description: What the top customer paid, in dollars.

top_customer_total_display.description: What the top customer paid as a person writes it, such as $1,234.50. Use it in a message.

total.description: Revenue in the currency's usual units, such as dollars.

total_display.description: The total as a person writes it, such as $1,234.50. Use it in a message.

list_payouts.description: List the money Stripe sent to your bank in a period, with the day each payout reaches the bank and its amount in dollars (or your currency), to check against your bank statement.
list_payouts.name: list_payouts

parameters.description: The start of the period, by the day money reaches the bank.
parameters.name: arrived_after

parameters.description: The end of the period. Leave empty to include every payout from the start on.
parameters.name: arrived_before

payouts.description: Each payout, with its id, amount in dollars (or your currency), currency, status, the day it reaches the bank (YYYY-MM-DD) and the text on your bank statement.

refund_payment.description: Give back all or part of a payment.
refund_payment.name: refund_payment

parameters.description: The payment to refund.
parameters.name: payment_intent_id

parameters.description: How much to give back, in cents, not dollars: 200 is $2.00. Leave empty to refund the whole payment.
parameters.name: amount

parameters.description: Beta. How much to give back, written as a person would (25.10, or $1,200.50 from a sheet's cell). It is turned into cents and rounded for you, so no step is needed to multiply by 100 first. If both are given, this one is used; leave both empty to refund the whole payment.
parameters.name: amount_in_dollars

returns.description: The refund: its id, amount in cents and status.

retrieve_customer.description: Get a customer's details, such as their name and email. The step fails when no customer is given, as for a guest checkout, so use it only for payments that have a customer.
retrieve_customer.name: retrieve_customer

parameters.description: The customer to get.
parameters.name: customer_id

returns.description: The customer: their id, email, name and the rest of what Stripe keeps about them.

update_customer.description: Change a customer's email, name, phone number or note. Only the fields you fill in change.
update_customer.name: update_customer

parameters.description: The customer to change.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: A new email address.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: A new full name or business name.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: A new note about the customer, replacing the old one. Only your team sees it, in Stripe.
parameters.name: description

parameters.description: A new phone number.
parameters.name: phone

returns.description: The customer as it now stands: their id, email, name and the rest of what Stripe keeps about them.

description: Take payments, send payment links, issue refunds and follow customers and subscriptions.

stripe_checkout_completed_trigger.description: Runs when a customer finishes a Stripe checkout page or payment link. Money from a bank debit may still be clearing.

output.amount_total: The total, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_total_display: The total as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.created: When the checkout started, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.customer: The customer's id, empty for a guest checkout.
output.customer_details: The buyer's email, name, phone and address as entered.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the session.
output.payment_intent: The payment's id, for a one-off payment.
output.payment_link: The Payment Link's id, when the checkout came from one.
output.payment_status: paid; unpaid while a slower method such as a bank debit is still clearing; or no_payment_required.
output.subscription: The subscription's id, when the checkout started one.

stripe_dispute_opened_trigger.description: Runs when a customer disputes a payment with their bank (a chargeback), with the amount, the reason and when your evidence is due.

output.amount: The amount disputed, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_display: The amount disputed as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.charge: The id of the charge being disputed (ch_...).
output.created: When the dispute was opened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.evidence_details: due_by: when your evidence must reach Stripe, as a Unix timestamp.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the dispute.
output.reason: Why the customer's bank says it's disputed, such as fraudulent or product_not_received.
output.status: Where it stands, such as needs_response or warning_needs_response.

stripe_invoice_paid_trigger.description: Runs when an invoice is paid in Stripe, including each subscription renewal and an invoice marked paid outside Stripe.

output.amount_due: The amount due, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_due_display: The amount due as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.amount_paid: The amount paid, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_paid_display: The amount paid as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.amount_remaining: What is still owed, in the currency's smallest unit.
output.amount_remaining_display: What is still owed as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.attempt_count: Which try this was: how many times Stripe has tried to collect payment.
output.created: When the invoice was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.hosted_invoice_url: The invoice's page, where the customer can pay it.
output.invoice_pdf: A link to download the invoice as a PDF.
output.next_payment_attempt: When Stripe tries again, as a Unix timestamp, if it will.
output.payer: Who the customer is, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'. Customer name is blank for some customers.
output.status: The status, such as paid or open.

stripe_invoice_payment_failed_trigger.description: Runs each time Stripe fails to collect an invoice, such as when a card is declined on a subscription renewal.

output.amount_due: The amount due, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_due_display: The amount due as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.amount_paid: The amount paid, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_paid_display: The amount paid as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.amount_remaining: What is still owed, in the currency's smallest unit.
output.amount_remaining_display: What is still owed as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.attempt_count: Which try this was: how many times Stripe has tried to collect payment.
output.created: When the invoice was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.hosted_invoice_url: The invoice's page, where the customer can pay it.
output.invoice_pdf: A link to download the invoice as a PDF.
output.next_payment_attempt: When Stripe tries again, as a Unix timestamp, if it will.
output.payer: Who the customer is, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'. Customer name is blank for some customers.
output.status: The status, such as paid or open.

stripe_new_customer_trigger.description: Runs when a customer is added in Stripe, whether by a checkout, an invoice, your team or another app.

output.created: When the customer was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.description: The description saved on the customer.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the customer.
output.name: Their name.

stripe_new_payment_trigger.description: Runs when someone pays you in Stripe or, with a status chosen, when a payment reaches that status.

output.amount: The amount in cents (or the currency's smallest unit), so 5000 is $50.00.
output.amount_display: The amount as a person writes it, such as $50.00.
output.created: When the payment was made, as a Unix timestamp. Make it a readable date before it goes in a sheet, email or message.
output.created_display: Beta. The day of the payment as a person writes it, such as Nov 6, 2026, ready for a sheet, email or message with no date step.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.customer: The customer's id, empty for a guest checkout.
output.customer_email: The payer's email, blank when Stripe doesn't know.
output.customer_name: Who paid, blank when Stripe doesn't know. To name the payer in a message or sheet, use payer instead.
output.description: The note saved on the payment, if any.
output.payer: Who paid, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a guest customer'.
output.status: The payment's state, such as succeeded or processing.

parameters.description: Only run for payments in this state, such as succeeded. Leave empty to run once for every new payment, including ones still waiting for the customer to pay.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Only run for payments of at least this much, in dollars (or your currency), not cents: 1000 means $1,000. Leave empty to run for every amount.
parameters.name: minimum_amount

stripe_new_subscription_trigger.description: Runs when a subscription starts in Stripe, including one that starts with a free trial.

output.cancel_at_period_end: Whether it is set to end when the period it is in ends.
output.canceled_at: When it was canceled, as a Unix timestamp, if it was.
output.cancellation_details: Why it ended: reason (cancellation_requested when the customer chose to leave, payment_failed when their payments kept failing, or payment_disputed), plus comment and feedback when the customer gave any. Read reason to tell a customer who left from one whose card failed.
output.created: When the subscription was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.customer_email: The customer's email address, blank when Stripe has none.
output.customer_name: The customer's name, blank when Stripe has none.
output.ended_at: When it ended, as a Unix timestamp, if it has.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.items: What is subscribed to: each item's price, product and quantity.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the subscription.
output.payer: Who the customer is, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'.
output.status: The status, such as active, trialing or canceled.

stripe_payment_failed_trigger.description: Beta. Runs when a one-off card payment fails in Stripe, such as a declined card at checkout, including payments with no invoice. For a failed subscription or invoice payment use Invoice payment failed.

output.amount: The amount, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_display: The amount as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.created: When the payment was started, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.customer: The customer's id, empty for a guest checkout.
output.description: The note saved on the payment, if any.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.last_payment_error: Why it failed: message (in words a person can read), code and decline_code, such as insufficient_funds.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the payment.
output.receipt_email: The email receipts go to, blank when none was given.
output.status: The payment's state, usually requires_payment_method after a failure.

stripe_payment_refunded_trigger.description: Runs each time a payment is refunded in Stripe, in full or in part, whether from the dashboard, Refund a payment or another app.

output.amount: What was paid, in the currency's smallest unit (cents).
output.amount_display: What was paid as a person writes it, such as $12.50.
output.amount_refunded: How much has been refunded so far, in cents.
output.amount_refunded_display: How much has been refunded so far, such as $12.50.
output.billing_details: The payer's name, email, phone and address as entered.
output.created: When the payment was made, as a Unix timestamp.
output.currency: The three-letter currency code, such as usd.
output.customer: The customer's id, empty for a guest checkout.
output.description: The note saved on the payment, if any.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.id: The charge's id (ch_...): the card payment that was refunded.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the payment.
output.receipt_email: The email receipts go to, blank when none was given.
output.refunded: Whether the whole payment has now been refunded.

stripe_subscription_ended_trigger.description: Runs when a subscription ends in Stripe: canceled straight away, at the end of its period, or after payments kept failing.

output.cancel_at_period_end: Whether it is set to end when the period it is in ends.
output.canceled_at: When it was canceled, as a Unix timestamp, if it was.
output.cancellation_details: Why it ended: reason (cancellation_requested when the customer chose to leave, payment_failed when their payments kept failing, or payment_disputed), plus comment and feedback when the customer gave any. Read reason to tell a customer who left from one whose card failed.
output.created: When the subscription was created, as a Unix timestamp.
output.customer_email: The customer's email address, blank when Stripe has none.
output.customer_name: The customer's name, blank when Stripe has none.
output.ended_at: When it ended, as a Unix timestamp, if it has.
output.event_created: When the event happened, as a Unix timestamp.
output.event_id: The id of the Stripe event (evt_...).
output.items: What is subscribed to: each item's price, product and quantity.
output.metadata: Your own key-value data saved on the subscription.
output.payer: Who the customer is, ready to put in a message: their name, else their email, else 'a customer'.
output.status: The status, such as active, trialing or canceled.
